hypothesis: For at least one of the system types named in the claim (Turing machines), a single uniform construction turns any one-dimensional cellular automaton rule (any number of colours k, any radius r) into a Turing machine that emulates it exactly; applied to rule 110 the construction yields an explicit Turing machine, which is then universal by the universality of rule 110 (Cook, Complex Systems 15 (2004) 1-40), so the system type contains a universal member as the claim asserts.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. analysis.py builds, for a given (k, r, rule table), a Turing machine whose tape holds the cellular-automaton configuration on W cells between two end-marker symbols, and whose head performs one left-to-right sweep (reading each old cell value once, carrying the last 2r old values in its state, stepping back r cells to write the new value) followed by a return to the left end, so that one round trip equals one cellular-automaton step with fixed white (0) boundaries. The machine must be a genuine finite table: every (state, symbol) pair reachable in the runs has exactly one transition writing one symbol and moving one cell. Tests: (a) all 256 elementary rules (k = 2, r = 1), W = 48, 40 steps, two random initial conditions each (seed 20261110); (b) 100 random 3-colour radius-1 rules (k = 3, r = 1), same W and steps; (c) 50 random 2-colour radius-2 rules (k = 2, r = 2); (d) 20 random 4-colour radius-1 rules and 10 random 3-colour radius-2 rules. After every round trip the tape between the markers is compared cell-for-cell with the directly computed cellular-automaton configuration (fixed-0 boundary). 'supports' if the total number of mismatching cells over all runs is 0 and the rule-110 machine is produced with a finite, fully specified state table (its state count and transition count reported).
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. 'refutes' if any run produces a mismatch (one or more cells differing from the direct evolution) that cannot be traced to a bug in the harness rather than the construction; since the construction is uniform in (k, r, rule), a single irreparable mismatch shows the uniform construction does not emulate every cellular automaton. 'inconclusive' with reason 'other' if the harness cannot complete the runs within the time budget.
interpretation: The claim is a logical implication (if a system type can emulate every cellular automaton and a universal cellular automaton exists, the type has universal members). The implication itself is not empirical; what can be checked computationally is its first premise for a concrete system type. We check it for Turing machines, the second family named in the claim, by implementing a uniform emulation construction (the sweeping-head scheme NKS describes for Turing machines emulating cellular automata, p. 665-666, written here from scratch rather than copied) and testing it exhaustively on the elementary rules and on random rules with more colours and larger neighbourhoods. The second premise (existence of a universal cellular automaton) is taken from the published proof that rule 110 is universal; it is not re-derived. The other families in the claim (mobile automata, substitution systems, tag and cyclic tag systems, symbolic systems, register machines) are not tested here, so a 'supports' verdict confirms the claim's structure for one family only.

datasets.name: Turing machines constructed by analysis.py from cellular-automaton rules (all 256 elementary rules; random rules with k in {2,3,4} and r in {1,2}, seed 20261110), run on W = 48 cells for 40 cellular-automaton steps and compared with direct evolution
datasets.role: the emulation premise of the implication, for the Turing-machine family
